title: Zero-Trust Onboarding Guide
summary: How every request is verified, every time, and what that means for your first week.
author: Security Engineering
body: Northwind follows a zero-trust model: network location never grants access. Every request to an internal service is evaluated against the policy for that service.
New starters receive a signed credential from the identity office. The credential lists role, department, clearance and device posture, and only the holder keeps it.
When you open an internal tool, the access gateway sends a fresh challenge. Your client proves that your credential satisfies the tool's policy without disclosing the credential itself.
Sessions last ten minutes. After that, or if the credential registry changes, you simply prove again.

title: Incident Response Runbook (v4)
summary: Severity levels, paging rules and the first 30 minutes of a security incident.
author: SRE Guild
body: SEV-1: customer-visible outage or confirmed data exposure. Page the incident commander immediately.
SEV-2: degraded service with a workaround. Open an incident channel within 15 minutes.
SEV-3: internal impact only. File a ticket and notify the owning team.
During the first 30 minutes: stabilise, communicate, preserve evidence. Do not rotate credentials before forensic snapshots are taken unless instructed.

title: Device Compliance Requirements
summary: Disk encryption, OS patch level and endpoint protection required for compliant devices.
author: Endpoint Team
body: Full-disk encryption must be enabled and escrowed.
Operating system patches older than 30 days make a device non-compliant.
Endpoint protection must report healthy within the last 24 hours.
Non-compliant devices can still reach the public intranet but not services whose policy requires a compliant device.

title: Release Train Calendar
summary: Fortnightly release cadence, code freeze windows and the hotfix process.
author: Release Management
body: Release branches are cut every second Tuesday at 10:00 UTC.
Code freeze begins 24 hours before the cut.
Hotfixes require approval from the on-call engineering manager and a linked incident.

title: Travel and Expense Policy
summary: What can be expensed, approval limits and receipt requirements.
author: Finance Operations
body: Economy class for flights under six hours.
Receipts are required for any expense above 25 EUR.
Managers approve up to 2,000 EUR; above that requires finance director sign-off.

title: Internal API Style Guide
summary: Naming, versioning, error envelopes and pagination for internal HTTP APIs.
author: Platform Team
body: Version APIs in the path: /v1/…
Errors use the envelope { error: { code, message } } with stable, machine-readable codes.
Large integers (field elements, IDs) are serialised as decimal strings, never JSON numbers.
Cursor-based pagination is preferred over offsets.

title: Office Access and Visitors
summary: Badge rules, visitor registration and lab access.
author: Workplace Services
body: Visitors must be registered 24 hours in advance.
Lab access requires a separate safety induction.
